registry: The Tank Guide University Research Library

evidence_relationship.research_basis: Listed in a section's 'Research basis:' line in the package.
evidence_relationship.research_basis_limited_scope: Listed in a 'Research basis:' line, with the package explicitly limiting what the source supports.
evidence_relationship.figure_data_source: Named as 'Source:' for a figure or table.
evidence_relationship.manufacturer_guidance: Manufacturer documentation cited for product features; not independent scientific evidence.
evidence_relationship.claim_audit_named_source: Named (by document or organization) in a Claim Audit editorial note, where the package key is unambiguous.
evidence_relationship.verification_replacement_source: Supplementary source added during an independent verification pass to support a claim whose original package citation was mismatched. Not an original package citation; does not replace or rewrite the historical citation record.
evidence_relationship.inline_citation: Named in an in-text parenthetical or sentence citation (author–year or title) that maps unambiguously to one bibliography entry.
evidence_relationship.named_source_restatement: The package restates a claim it explicitly cites elsewhere, naming the organization but not the specific document at this location; mapped via the explicit citation and flagged for confirmation.
evidence_relationship.collective_reference: The package points to a body of work ('… and colleagues … see the bibliography') without naming individual works; the entry is a candidate member.
evidence_relationship.bibliography_annotation: Tied to the claim by the bibliography entry's own parenthetical annotation rather than an in-text citation.
evidence_relationship.hobbyist_source_bibliography_annotation: Hobbyist/community or grouped hobby source tied to a claim or topic by its bibliography annotation; per the package, not scientific evidence.
evidence_relationship.manufacturer_product_named: Manufacturer product named in the text as an example; not independent evidence.
evidence_relationship.manufacturer_claim_reproduced: Manufacturer figure reproduced by the package as a manufacturer claim; the package discloses it was not independently verified.
evidence_relationship.bibliography_listing_only: Listed in the package bibliography but not tied to any specific claim (purely descriptive relationship).

vocabularies.package_evidence_status: Verbatim Claim Audit status(es) from package Section 12 that apply to the claim; NOT_RATED_IN_CLAIM_AUDIT when the section has no Claim Audit row.

support_status.direct_support: The source directly states what the package uses it for.
support_status.partial_support: The source directly supports part of the cited claim but not all of it.
support_status.background_support: The source provides general context but does not state the specific claim.
support_status.practical_translation: The source establishes the underlying principle; the package's specific recommendation is a Tank Guide practical application, not something the source directly tested or prescribes.
support_status.limited_analogy: The source addresses a different context (e.g., human emergency water) and is used only as an analogy.
support_status.manufacturer_feature_documentation: Official manufacturer documentation verifying model-specific features only; not independent evidence.
support_status.unsupported_or_mismatched: The source is legitimate but does not support this specific claim strongly enough. The historical citation is preserved.
support_status.needs_review: Support has not yet been assessed.
support_status.not_applicable_listing_only: Purely descriptive relationship (source listed in the bibliography but not tied to a claim); support strength does not apply.

vocabularies.replacement_source_needed: Boolean. true when the cited source does not adequately support the claim and a replacement or additional source is required before the claim is represented publicly as externally supported.
vocabularies.support_reason: Verification-pass explanation of the assigned support_status (null when none was recorded).
vocabularies.evidence_relationship_note: evidence_relationship records how the package cited the source (historical fact) and is never changed by verification; support_status separately records how well the source supports that use.
vocabularies.replacement_source_ids: Supplementary source IDs that now provide verified support for a claim whose original citation remains unsupported_or_mismatched.

package_evidence_status_by_package.PKG-2026-08-gh-kh-ph: Verbatim evidence tag(s) the package attaches to the claim where the citation appears — from its Evidence Classification Key ([EST], [STR], [INF], [AQC], [VET], [HOB], [ANC], [CON], [MYTH], including compound/variant forms), or the verbatim Section 32 'Classification:' text for Section 32 claims. 'UNTAGGED_IN_PACKAGE' when the claim carries no explicit tag; null for listing-only relationships. package_evidence_status_note explains mixed or inherited tags.

vocabularies.bibliography_tier: PKG-2026-08-gh-kh-ph only: the verbatim bibliography tier heading under which the package lists the source.

usage.original_package_key: Wurts, W. A., & Durborow, R. M. (1992)
usage.section_or_claim: Section 1.1 — What pH Measures (pH as the negative base-10 logarithm of hydrogen ion concentration)
usage.citation_statement: the SRAC fact sheet frames pH as an index of the hydrogen ion concentration in water, formally the negative base-10 logarithm of the molar concentration of H⁺ (Wurts & Durborow, 1992, SRAC 464).

usage.original_package_key: Merck Veterinary Manual. Environmental Diseases of Aquatic Animals in Aquatic Systems
usage.section_or_claim: Section 1.6 — Why pH Changes Over the Course of a Day (diurnal CO₂/pH cycling in plant- or algae-containing systems)
usage.citation_statement: the Merck Veterinary Manual describes CO₂ in plant- or algae-containing systems as cycling on a daily basis, with daytime photosynthesis pulling CO₂ down and pushing pH up, and overnight respiration reversing both (Merck Veterinary Manual, Environmental Diseases of Aquatic Animals in Aquatic Systems).

usage.original_package_key: Wurts, W. A., & Durborow, R. M. (1992)
usage.section_or_claim: Section 1.6 — Magnitude depends on alkalinity (ponds under ~20 mg/L total alkalinity swinging roughly pH 6–10 within a day; stress, depressed growth, mortality)
usage.citation_statement: The Southern Regional Aquaculture Center reports that ponds holding less than about 20 mg/L total alkalinity as CaCO₃ can swing across roughly pH 6 to pH 10 within a single day, and that swings of that size are associated with stress, depressed growth, and mortality in farmed aquatic animals (Wurts & Durborow, 1992; Wurts & Masser, 2013, SRAC 4100).
notes: Package caveat in the same section: 'The mechanism transfers; the magnitude does not.' The 20 mg/L ≈ 1.1 dKH aquarium translation that follows is tagged [INF].

usage.original_package_key: Wurts, W. A., & Masser, M. P. (2013)
usage.section_or_claim: Section 1.6 — Magnitude depends on alkalinity (ponds under ~20 mg/L total alkalinity swinging roughly pH 6–10 within a day; stress, depressed growth, mortality)
usage.citation_statement: (Wurts & Durborow, 1992; Wurts & Masser, 2013, SRAC 4100)
notes: Co-cited with SRAC 464; the package does not assign separate parts of the statement to each source.
See the SRAC 4100 source record for the title/URL discrepancy as given in the package.

usage.original_package_key: U.S. Geological Survey. Hardness of Water
usage.section_or_claim: Section 2.1 — What GH Measures (hardness as essentially the quantity of dissolved calcium and magnesium)
usage.citation_statement: The US Geological Survey defines it in these terms: hardness is, in scientific terms, essentially the quantity of dissolved calcium and magnesium present (USGS, Hardness of Water).

usage.original_package_key: U.S. Geological Survey. Do you have information about water hardness in the United States?
usage.section_or_claim: Section 2.2 — Units of GH: USGS classification (soft/moderately hard/hard/very hard bands; EPA sets no legal limit for hardness)
usage.citation_statement: the USGS uses four descriptive bands measured as calcium carbonate — soft at 0–60 mg/L, moderately hard at 61–120 mg/L, hard at 121–180 mg/L, and very hard above 180 mg/L. The USGS also notes that the EPA sets no legal limit for hardness, because the ions responsible are not toxic (USGS FAQ, Do you have information about water hardness in the United States?, updated 5 August 2025).
notes: The same bands supply the 'USGS descriptive category' column of the Section 2.2 conversion table and the 'USGS category' labels in worked examples in Sections 2.3 (p. 12) and 25.3 (p. 62).
Package caveat in the same section: the USGS categories were built for drinking water and household plumbing and 'should be used descriptively, not prescriptively.'

usage.original_package_key: Nguyen, et al. (2019)
usage.section_or_claim: Section 2.5.1 — Calcium in fish: reduction of gill permeability (Ca²⁺ at gill tight junctions; H⁺ displacement at low pH)
usage.citation_statement: the working model in the literature is that Ca²⁺ occupies binding sites at gill tight junctions and thereby lowers paracellular ion permeability, and that hydrogen ions at low pH displace that calcium, making the junctions leakier and accelerating ion loss (see e.g. Nguyen et al., 2019, Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology; reviews by Hunn, 1985 and Wood, 1989).
notes: The same sentence also cites 'reviews by Hunn, 1985 and Wood, 1989', neither of which appears in the bibliography; they are recorded at package level (in_text_citations_without_bibliography_entry) and not registered as sources.

usage.original_package_key: Eddy, F. B. (1975)
usage.section_or_claim: Section 2.5.1 — Calcium in fish: classic goldfish work (calcium cuts Na⁺/Cl⁻ efflux; transepithelial potential −10 mV to +10 mV)
usage.citation_statement: In classic work on goldfish, adding calcium to the water sharply cut both sodium and chloride efflux, and swung the transepithelial potential from roughly −10 mV in calcium-free medium to roughly +10 mV at 10 mM calcium (Eddy, 1975, Journal of Comparative Physiology A).

usage.original_package_key: Gonzalez, R. J., & Wilson, R. W. (2001)
usage.section_or_claim: Section 2.5.1 — Critical species-specific caveat: the calcium-tightens-gills model is not universal in Amazonian characids and cichlids
usage.citation_statement: across both characids and cichlids, sodium efflux resists stimulation by acid exposure to a degree that temperate models do not predict (Gonzalez and colleagues, 1997–2021; summarised in Gonzalez & Wilson, 2001 and subsequent work).
notes: The package describes this as 'one of the most important nuances in this entire document.'
'Gonzalez and colleagues, 1997–2021' spans works outside the bibliography's listed Gonzalez entries (2001, 2002, 2005); only Gonzalez & Wilson (2001) is named here.

usage.original_package_key: Platek, A., et al. (2017)
usage.section_or_claim: Section 2.5.1 — Environmental calcium also affects gill morphology (mangrove rivulus interlamellar cell mass)
usage.citation_statement: in mangrove rivulus, fish held in naturally hard water carried a shorter interlamellar cell mass than fish in low-calcium water, and restoring calcium to low-calcium water brought gill surface area back — identifying environmental calcium as an ionic trigger for gill remodeling (Platek et al., 2017, Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A).
